questions.q: What is a minimal viable experiment (MVE), as defined in this lesson?
options: The most thorough version of the experiment you can afford to run
The smallest version of the experiment that could still answer the research question
A pilot study with no baseline comparison
An experiment run only after the full version fails
questions.explain: An MVE is the cheapest version of an experiment that still produces evidence toward the research question — not the most thorough version imaginable.

questions.q: This lesson gives a specific MVE example for Project 1. What is it?
options: Tune all six actions against every possible query shape
Train PPO on one query template for 50,000 timesteps, then compare 200 held-out episodes against the optimizer's default plan
Run the optimizer alone with no agent for a baseline-only study
Train on AdventureWorks2012 and Northwind simultaneously
questions.explain: The lesson frames Project 1's MVE as training PPO on one query template for 50,000 timesteps and evaluating against 200 held-out episodes versus the optimizer's default plan.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say a time-box has to be decided before you start, not after you're already behind?
options: Because you can only think clearly about what 'good enough' looks like before you're inside the deadline pressure
Because course software automatically locks the deadline
Because time-boxes are only a formality with no real effect
Because it has to match the length of every other lesson
questions.explain: A time-box only works if it's decided before you're inside it, when you can still think clearly — deciding it under pressure defeats the purpose.

questions.q: In the risk register example, what is the suggested mitigation for scope creep, like adding 'just one more hint type'?
options: Add the new idea immediately since it might improve results
Freeze the action space in the MVE template before training starts
Extend the time-box to accommodate it
Switch research questions entirely
questions.explain: The risk register's mitigation for scope creep is freezing the action space in the MVE template before training begins, rather than expanding it mid-project.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what does a null result reached inside the time-box count as?
options: A failed project that should not be written up
A finished project, since the result still answers the research question
A sign the research question was chosen incorrectly
Grounds to restart the project with a new baseline
questions.explain: A null result is an answer to the research question, not a failure — reached on time, it counts as a finished project and belongs in the write-up.
